description: Sabotages for windows-namespace-request-sys's allocation-failure paths (NR-3): an allocation that fails is an error the caller receives, never a panic or an abort. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.
notCoveredHere: The allocation-failure paths (NR-3) and the device-control helper with its first entry (NR-2.1) have entries. The catalogue's other entries, the capture of handles and paths, and the security descriptor's own parsing are not covered. SecurityDescriptor::try_clone's failure is a declared blind spot (see its survives entry): AlignedBuf::try_clone allocates exactly the size of a buffer that already exists, so no test can make it fail. The pending path of the device-control helper (the wait, the abort, the result read after it) has no entry, and the reason is a measurement rather than a gap: an overlapped call pended in 0 of 20000 isolated runs of the two controls tried, and appeared only while the whole suite ran in parallel, so a mutation confined to it is caught on some runs and survives on others, and neither outcome is a control. Only a control that pends on demand would settle it, and none taking no input is known: FSCTL_PIPE_LISTEN, the obvious one, failed with ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION through DeviceIoControl on a named-pipe server, for a reason not established. The failures of the two descriptor allocations, in capture and in conversion, are reached through their shared function, `allocate`, which the tests call with a length no machine has; the OS names the real length, so no descriptor can be made to ask for it.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a capacity the machine cannot supply is reported under another code
sabotages.why: A query whose buffer cannot be allocated reports ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, the code a caller reads as 'ask for less'. Any other code would read as the call's own failure.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor allocation failure is reported as an invalid copy
sabotages.why: An allocation failure is its own failure, SecurityCaptureFailure::Allocate: an invalid copy would send a caller looking for a malformed descriptor.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor allocation failure carries the wrong code
sabotages.why: The error's raw code is ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, which a caller who funnels everything through raw_os_error reads as 'out of memory'.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a copy of security attributes drops the descriptor
sabotages.why: A copy that kept the inheritance choice but not the descriptor would open files with different security than the original.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a failed security copy is reported as a failed duplication
sabotages.why: A request's try_clone reports a failed copy of its security attributes as HandleCaptureFailure::CopySecurity, not as DuplicateHandle, which would send a caller looking at a handle that was never the problem.

sabotages.name: NR-3: an open request's copy forgets its security attributes
sabotages.why: The copy must open with what the original would; the attributes went through Clone before, and nothing but this test would notice a copy that dropped them.

sabotages.name: NR-3: an open-by-identifier request's copy forgets its security attributes
sabotages.why: As for the path-named open: the copy must carry the attributes the original does.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor alignment that is not a power of two is refused by the build
sabotages.why: AlignedBuf refuses such an alignment and `allocate` reports every refusal as an allocation failure, so a bad constant would read as out of memory on every call. The constant is asserted where it is defined.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a batch alignment that is not a power of two is refused by the build
sabotages.why: As for the descriptor's: `perform` reports every refusal of the allocation as ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, so a bad constant would be misreported as out of memory.

sabotages.name: NR-3: BLIND SPOT: a failed copy of a descriptor is reported as an invalid copy
sabotages.why: Declared blind spot, not a control. SecurityDescriptor::try_clone allocates exactly the size of a buffer that already exists, so no test can make it fail; the failure it would report is the shared `allocation()`, whose result the other entries pin.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: the event handed to an overlapped control does not suppress the completion packet
sabotages.why: A handle on a completion port gets a packet when an overlapped call completes unless the event's low bit is set. Without it a control would reach a consumer's loop as a completion it never asked for.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a control is told its output buffer is empty
sabotages.why: The buffer length the device is given is the buffer's own; a shorter one makes every control fail for want of room.
find:
DeviceIoControl(
                device,
                code,
                ptr::null(),
                0,
                output.as_mut_ptr().cast(),
                output_len,
replace:
DeviceIoControl(
                device,
                code,
                ptr::null(),
                0,
                output.as_mut_ptr().cast(),
                output_len - output_len,

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a control that completed reports no bytes written
sabotages.why: The byte count is what a caller checks the reply's size by; a count of nothing would read as an empty reply.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a reply larger than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: A reply of any size but the structure's is reported and not read, because a value taken from a buffer the device did not fill would read as a node.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a reply smaller than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: The other half of the size check: a short reply leaves the buffer's remainder as it was, and reading it would report a node the device never named.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: the node is read from the first byte alone
sabotages.why: The node is a whole ULONG, carried unaltered; a value above 255 would be truncated.
